name: Chicken Foot
description: Chicken Foot is a domino game that originated in Texas or Mexico. It is a variation of Maltese Cross played with a double-9 or larger domino set. The game gets its name from the shape formed when a double is played - the next three tiles must be played on the double, creating a chicken foot shape.
deck: Double-9 domino set (55 tiles) or larger

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Texas/Mexico
Time Period: Late 20th century
Historical Development: Developed as a variation of Maltese Cross dominoes. The distinctive 'chicken foot' shape created by playing on doubles gives the game its name.
Cultural Significance: Popular domino game in the southern United States and Mexico. Often played socially in homes and community gatherings.
timeline: Late 20th century: Originated in Texas/Mexico region
Evolution: Developed from Maltese Cross dominoes
Modern Era: Popular throughout USA and internationally
Variations: Played with double-9, double-12, or larger sets
history.cultural: The name comes from the visual appearance of the domino layout when a double is played - the three tiles played on it resemble a chicken's foot. The game is often played in boisterous, social settings.
history.evolution: The game started with double-9 sets but is often played with double-12 sets for more players or longer games. Tournament rules have formalized some aspects of play.

rules.objective: Be the first player to play all your dominoes. Score points based on opponents' remaining tiles. First to reach target score (usually 100 or 150) wins.
rules.gameplay: The player with the highest double (9-9 with double-9 set) starts. If not drawn, all players draw one extra tile until found. The first double played starts the 'spinner' with four arms. Subsequent doubles are played crosswise and are 'spinners' - the next three plays must be on the double, creating a chicken foot. After three tiles are played on a double, the arm can be extended normally. Players unable to play draw from the chicken yard. If still unable to play, they pass.
keyRules: Highest double starts (9-9 for double-9 set)
First double is the spinner with four arms
After a double is played, next three plays must be on it (chicken foot)
Chicken foot must be completed before extending other arms
If unable to play, draw from chicken yard
If still unable after drawing, pass
Round ends when player empties hand or game is blocked

strategy.basic: Try to play doubles early to create chicken feet and control the board. Get rid of high-pip tiles quickly to minimize points if opponent dominoes. Save tiles that can play on likely doubles.
strategy.intermediate: Pay attention to which doubles have been played and which remain. Force opponents to draw by playing doubles when you have tiles to continue the foot. Block opponents by completing chicken feet they can't extend.
strategy.advanced: Sophisticated tile counting to track what opponents hold. Strategic use of doubles to force opponents to pass. Managing hand composition for endgame. Recognizing when to play defensively versus aggressively.
tips: Play the double-blank tile early so you don't get stuck with it
Doubles are powerful - use them strategically
Watch which doubles haven't been played
Try to have a tile that can play on a new double
When an opponent has one tile left, play a double to force them to draw
Keep track of high-value tiles played
Balance completing chicken feet with advancing your own position
